19 A car of mass 500 kg is at rest at point X on a slope, as shown.
The car’s brakes are released and the car rolls down the slope with its engine switched off. At
point Y the car has moved through a vertical height of 30 m and has a speed of 11 m s–1.
mass = 500 kg
speed = 0 m s–1
X
speed = 11 m s–1
30 m
Y
What is the energy dissipated by frictional forces when the car moves from X to Y?
A
3.0 × 104
J
B
1.2 × 105
J
C
1.5 × 105
J
D
1.8 × 105
J

hints: Notice the car starts from rest at X with vertical height 30 m above Y, so calculate the gravitational potential energy lost as $mgh$ with $m = 500 \text{ kg}$.
Connect the missing energy to friction: with the engine off, lost potential energy becomes kinetic energy plus work done against frictional forces.
Calculate the kinetic energy at Y from $\frac{1}{2}mv^2$ with $v = 11 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, then subtract it from the $mgh$ value to leave the dissipated energy.
walkthrough: Identify the energy store at X: the car is at rest so kinetic energy is zero, but it has gravitational potential energy relative to Y because $h = 30 \text{ m}$.
Calculate the potential energy lost from X to Y using $\Delta E_p = mgh = 500 \times 9.81 \times 30 \approx 1.47 \times 10^5 \text{ J}$.
Calculate the kinetic energy gained at Y using $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 = 0.5 \times 500 \times (11)^2 = 250 \times 121 = 30250 \text{ J}$.
Apply conservation of energy with friction: $mgh = E_k + W_{friction}$, so dissipated energy $W_{friction} = mgh - E_k$.
Substitute: $W_{friction} \approx 147000 - 30000 = 117000 \text{ J} \approx 1.2 \times 10^5 \text{ J}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: This is the final kinetic energy at Y, $\frac{1}{2}mv^2$, not the energy lost to friction.

B.explanation: This is the loss of gravitational potential energy minus the kinetic energy gained at Y, which equals work done against friction.

C.explanation: This is the loss of gravitational potential energy $mgh$ only, before subtracting the kinetic energy still stored in the car.

D.explanation: This adds kinetic energy to potential energy, whereas friction removes energy so the dissipated energy is the difference.
